prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1137; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant, who reports a side impact at a signalized intersection while proceeding through on a green light. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has asked for guidance on the claim process.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member. Coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who described the collision the same way the claimant did. Photos from the scene show the damage on the driver's side of the claimant's vehicle.

Entry 4: Police report obtained. Officers confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene and note the positions of both cars consistent with a side impact.

Entry 5: Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the sequence of events reported by both drivers. Neither witness has any known connection to the parties.

Entry 6: Repair estimate received. The location and pattern of damage on the claimant's vehicle match the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 7: Claimant reports neck and back strain following the collision and was evaluated at an urgent care clinic the same day. Records are requested to confirm the diagnosis.

Entry 8: Claimant has described the accident and symptoms the same way in each call and written statement so far. Nothing in the account has changed between conversations.

Entry 9: Medical review is still open. It is not yet clear whether the neck and back complaints came from this crash, as the claimant's records need to be compared with the timeline of symptoms.

Entry 10: Treatment records show a usual course of care, including physical therapy and medication, with visits tapering as the claimant improved. Billing reviewed and appears consistent with the treatment notes.

Entry 11: Prior records show the claimant had a minor strain in the same area years ago that healed fully with no ongoing care. The history is noted for the medical reviewer, who will consider it alongside the current findings.

Entry 12: File under review. Liability appears clear based on the police report, witness statements, and damage pattern. Injury evaluation remains pending the medical reviewer's opinion on causation.
